package_info.package_versions: Multiple MSI motherboard models (potentially all affected by leaked keys)
package_info.why_malicious: The leak of highly sensitive cryptographic Boot Guard signing keys allows attackers to sign malicious firmware or bootkits that will be trusted by the platform's secure boot process. This enables attackers to install persistent, stealthy malware at the firmware level, bypassing all operating system and endpoint security controls, and undermining the hardware root of trust.

execution_context.file_location: UEFI/BIOS firmware image on motherboard flash storage
required_permissions: firmware write access (physical or privileged software access)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Malicious bootkit or firmware image, cryptographically signed with leaked MSI Boot Guard private key, containing code to subvert OS security and enable persistent compromise.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At system boot, the malicious firmware image executes as a signed bootkit, initializes before the operating system loads, intercepts or modifies boot process data flows, and establishes persistent, stealthy control over the system, enabling further attacks such as credential theft or rootkit installation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Firmware images signed with OEM private keys but not issued by the OEM are highly suspicious, as they can bypass secure boot and hardware attestation, allowing attackers to run arbitrary code with the highest privileges before the OS loads.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, only the OEM can sign firmware or bootloader updates, ensuring only trusted code runs at boot. The use of leaked signing keys allows attackers to sign and install malicious firmware that is accepted as legitimate, breaking the secure boot trust model.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate firmware updates or security patches signed and distributed by the OEM to add features or fix vulnerabilities.
key_indicators: Firmware or bootloader images signed with MSI Boot Guard keys known to be leaked
Unexpected or unauthorized firmware updates detected on systems
Bootkits or firmware that pass secure boot validation but are not issued by the OEM
Discrepancies in secure boot logs or hardware attestation results

attack_chain.action: Attacker acquires leaked MSI Boot Guard signing keys from underground forums or data leaks.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ability to cryptographically sign malicious firmware or bootkits that will be trusted by secure boot.

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a malicious bootkit or firmware image and signs it with the leaked MSI Boot Guard key.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious firmware appears authentic and is accepted by secure boot, bypassing firmware integrity checks.

attack_chain.action: Malicious firmware is delivered and installed on the target system via physical access, supply chain compromise, or remote firmware update exploit.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious bootkit is present on the system and will execute at next boot.

attack_chain.action: On system boot, the malicious bootkit executes with highest privileges, subverting OS security and enabling persistent compromise (e.g., credential theft, rootkit installation, disabling security features).
attack_chain.leads_to: Full system compromise that is extremely difficult to detect or remediate, as the malware operates below the OS.

behavioral_signatures: Firmware or bootloader images cryptographically signed with MSI Boot Guard keys known to be leaked
Unexpected or unauthorized firmware updates or changes detected on endpoints
Boot-time code execution that bypasses or disables OS-level security controls
Anomalies in secure boot logs or hardware attestation results indicating firmware tampering
file_indicators: UEFI/BIOS firmware images with digital signatures matching the leaked MSI Boot Guard keys
Firmware update files not matching official MSI release hashes or signatures
Presence of unauthorized firmware update utilities or tools
network_indicators: N/A (primary attack is local/firmware-level; however, post-compromise, the system may initiate C2 traffic or exfiltrate data once the OS is subverted)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for firmware or bootloader images signed with the leaked MSI Boot Guard keys using hardware attestation and secure boot log analysis. Alert on any firmware updates or changes that do not match official MSI release signatures or hashes. Implement out-of-band firmware integrity checks using a hardware root of trust. Investigate any anomalies in secure boot logs or attestation results. After compromise, monitor for unusual outbound network connections from affected systems.
